steps.title: Lasting over time
steps.text: Stability is the resistance of a stone to its environment: light, heat, chemicals and humidity. It is the third form of durability, with hardness and toughness. A hard, tough stone can still change colour or break down with time.

steps.title: Light
steps.text: Some colours fade in light: kunzite, amethyst, some yellow sapphires, some pink tourmalines. Long exposure to the sun dulls them. These stones are kept away from light and avoided in jewellery that is always exposed.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat can change the colour (a heated amethyst turns yellow), crack a stone (a thermal shock breaks topaz), soften amber or dry out opal, which then crazes. Heating is also a treatment: you must know that a stone that has been heated too much is no longer the same.

steps.title: Chemicals and humidity
steps.text:
Acids, perfumes, hairsprays and cleaning products attack soft or porous stones: pearl, coral, turquoise, opal. Even sweat dulls them in the long run.

Oiled or resin-filled emeralds do not tolerate an ultrasonic bath either, which drives the filling out.

steps.title: To remember
steps.text: • Stability covers light, heat, chemicals and humidity. • The three forms of durability are: hardness (scratches), toughness (blows) and stability (environment). • A beautiful stone is judged on all three: this decides the piece of jewellery it is set in.
